title: Restore resumed sessions through the canonical persisted runtime route
before: At parent 7fd2f574132fcf8aea71ca485ca489c367fedffe, the desktop/TUI resume reader extracted provider, base_url, and api_mode only from top-level model_config keys, then fell back to billing_provider. It did not read model_config.gateway_runtime, even though gateway turns persisted their latest actual provider route there and CLI resume already consumed it through SessionDB.session_gateway_runtime. Consequently, a session whose provider changed through the messaging gateway could resume with its current stored model combined with a stale first-call billing provider or stale top-level route. The shared reader also returned any nonempty top-level route before consulting billing_provider, so delegating to it without adjustment would lose the established fallback that fills a missing top-level provider.
after: At 33c6ab002d1fac653d7e772025ef7aaab7c83480, the desktop/TUI resume reader delegates provider, base_url, and api_mode recovery to SessionDB.session_gateway_runtime. That canonical reader prioritizes a provider-bearing nested gateway_runtime, then top-level route fields, and uses a routable billing_provider only to fill a missing provider without overwriting explicit top-level data. CLI and desktop/TUI resume therefore interpret persisted route precedence consistently while retaining bare-billing-bucket filtering and legacy fallback behavior.
diff: The change removes the desktop/TUI reader's duplicated top-level-field and billing-provider resolution, replacing it with a call to the shared session route reader. The shared reader changes billing fallback from a separate last-choice return into setdefault on the accumulated top-level route, preserving top-level endpoint/interface fields while filling only a missing provider. Two regression tests cover a nested latest route conflicting respectively with a frozen billing provider and stale top-level route fields. The focused test file passes 4/4 at the implementation ref; when the two new tests are copied to the parent, those two fail with stale 'anthropic' routing while the two pre-existing cases pass.

title: Adapt outbound reasoning fields to a strict OpenAI-compatible endpoint
before: At parent d50dc84e363f4225193418fcd8844fa21f3ae66a, provider selection had no endpoint-specific branch for api.fireworks.ai, so those configurations fell through to the default OpenAI-compatible provider. For any request whose model name contained "qwen3", that provider copied a non-empty assistant message reasoning_content value into reasoning. Replayed thinking history was therefore sent with both fields, although the target endpoint accepted reasoning_content and rejected reasoning as an extra input, causing HTTP 400 failures on multi-turn and tool-call continuations.
after: At 3ba01990e13e9e8e14e147b60add50e0f972431a, configurations whose parsed hostname is api.fireworks.ai or a true subdomain select a dedicated provider. After applying normal default-provider transformations, that provider creates an outbound message array that removes reasoning only when it is a string exactly equal to reasoning_content on an assistant message. It preserves reasoning_content, distinct caller-supplied reasoning values, source conversation history, and existing behavior for other endpoints.
diff: The change adds and exports a dedicated OpenAI-compatible provider, inserts hostname-based provider routing before the default fallback, and overrides request construction to reverse only the default provider's recognizable reasoning mirror at the outbound boundary. It also adds focused routing and field-preservation tests plus an HTTP integration test that exercises conversion of replayed thought history through provider request construction to a strict endpoint stand-in. Four files changed with 407 insertions.

evidence_units.claim: Commit 3ba01990 resolves issue #11657 through PR #11701 and records parent d50dc84e363f4225193418fcd8844fa21f3ae66a, four changed files, and the failure mechanism: the endpoint rejects messages[N].reasoning while accepting reasoning_content.

In the parent state, the default provider recognized model names containing qwen3 and mapped assistant messages through mirrorReasoningContentToReasoning, which copied a non-empty reasoning_content string into reasoning when reasoning was not already a string.
The provider selector gained a branch before the default fallback that constructs the dedicated provider when its endpoint predicate matches.

Endpoint recognition parses baseUrl, lowercases the URL hostname, accepts the exact canonical hostname or dot-delimited subdomains, and returns false for absent or malformed URLs; it deliberately does not route by model name.
The endpoint-specific provider first invokes default request construction, then maps the resulting messages through an unmirroring operation without modifying the input request object.

Unmirroring applies only to assistant messages and removes reasoning only when it is a string equal to reasoning_content; non-assistant messages, unequal values, and non-string values are returned unchanged.
The request pipeline invokes provider.buildRequest after constructing the base request and before request capture and SDK execution, making the provider hook an outbound wire-shape boundary.

Conversation conversion serializes model thought parts into assistant reasoning_content before provider request construction, establishing how replayed thinking history reaches the mirroring and unmirroring logic.

Focused tests verify removal of the mirrored field while preserving reasoning_content and source history, recognition of a legitimate subdomain, rejection of a hostile suffix hostname, preservation of a distinct explicit reasoning value, and unchanged mirroring for a non-matching endpoint.

An HTTP strict-endpoint stand-in rejects any assistant reasoning field with a 400-shaped response; the end-to-end test sends an initial turn and a replayed-thinking continuation through the real generator/converter/provider path, receives successful responses, and asserts that reasoning_content but not reasoning reached the wire.
The new provider is exported from the provider barrel and the public openaiContentGenerator module, making it available to the selector and direct construction used by integration tests.

title: Adapt content-generation client configuration to provider-specific endpoint overrides
before: At parent c5ad0abb5de461416306a516ddbb26dc78f87d40, the content-generator adapter only copied an explicitly supplied config.baseUrl into SDK httpOptions, did not consult GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL or GOOGLE_VERTEX_BASE_URL, did not validate custom endpoint URLs, and forwarded config.vertexai unchanged; consequently provider mode could remain undefined when the selected authentication type identified Vertex AI but credentials had not populated the flag.
after: At cb289e0724b46ce867b6d3fe4bd0ac6ed890dc45, the adapter gives an explicit baseUrl precedence, otherwise selects the endpoint environment variable associated with the authentication type, validates every selected custom URL as parseable and HTTPS except for loopback hosts, passes the resolved URL through SDK httpOptions, and infers the SDK vertexai flag from the selected authentication type when no explicit flag is present.
diff: The implementation adds a custom-base-URL validator, provider-aware environment fallback and explicit-over-environment precedence, plus authentication-type fallback for the SDK provider-mode flag. Seven focused tests cover both provider endpoint variables, provider selection without inferred credentials, precedence, loopback HTTP, malformed URLs, and insecure remote HTTP; existing API-key expectations are updated from an undefined provider flag to false. Configuration documentation adds the two endpoint variables and their security constraints.

commit.body_excerpt:
* fix(auth): let Vertex AI authenticate with Application Default Credentials

Vertex AI auth required an API key, so an ADC or service account setup
could not start. Supplying a placeholder to satisfy the check made it
worse: an explicitly passed key switches the Google SDK to Vertex
Express mode, which clears the project and location and rejects the
request with "API keys are not supported by this API".

Treat a configured GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT as sufficient credentials for
the vertex-ai auth type, in both the CLI pre-flight check and the core
model config validation, and leave the API key absent so the SDK
resolves ADC itself. The missing-credentials errors now mention the
keyless path instead of pointing only at envKey.

Fixes #9016

evidence_units.claim: Pinned commit f743ab579098f982d87ea3f2472c2405f6999297 has parent c776c665b00a39d55c470beb788a2b9a77a2feb7, is titled "fix(core): sequentially verify cached credentials and restore GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS fallback (#28472)", and modifies the OAuth implementation and its tests.

Before the change, fetchCachedCredentials returned immediately on the first parseable credential object; the ordered paths placed the default cache before GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, and encrypted storage was returned directly.

Before the change, initOauthClient verified only the single credential returned by fetchCachedCredentials; a caught verification failure then proceeded to later interactive or compute authentication logic rather than another file credential.

The replacement fetchCachedCredentialsList accumulates credentials in priority order, isolates load and parse failures per source, includes GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS after the default file when unencrypted storage is used, and returns all successfully parsed candidates.

initOauthClient now iterates through the ordered candidate list. Non-authorized-user typed credentials are adapted through GoogleAuth, while OAuth credentials are assigned to a newly configured OAuth2 client and checked with getAccessToken plus getTokenInfo. Errors are caught per candidate so the loop can continue.

A shared OAuth2-client factory preserves proxy configuration, token persistence, and post-authentication callbacks for the access-token override, every OAuth credential candidate, and later authentication flows.

The public getOauthClient entry point memoizes and invokes initOauthClient, so callers of the existing authentication API receive the revised ordered resolution behavior without an API signature change.

Existing credential-order tests establish that a valid default cache remains preferred, GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS is used when the default is missing, and typed external credentials are adapted through GoogleAuth.

The added regression test creates an expired default refresh token and a valid environment-file refresh token, makes token verification reject the default, invokes getOauthClient, and asserts that the environment credential is eventually assigned.

The committed regression oracle verifies the repaired transition from invalid higher-priority credentials to valid lower-priority credentials while the neighboring tests guard the intended priority and credential-type behavior. title: Retry transient compaction and branch-summary failures under the configured retry budget
before: At parent 4b91ec66fd33026e6e44a0dca5a954a59abd3ee9, compaction, split-turn summarization, and branch summarization each issued one assistant completion request. A transient stream or transport error such as "terminated" immediately failed the summarization and therefore the enclosing context-compaction or branch-navigation operation. Existing assistant-turn retry settings were not applied to these internal summarization requests, and no summarization-specific retry lifecycle events were exposed.
after: At merge commit 65dd2e0ed6c71bd61d698353c29f2de24968bf76, all compaction and branch-summary completion paths pass through a reusable bounded retry operation. It applies the configured retry policy only to errors classified as transient, uses exponential backoff, stops at maxRetries, returns quota/billing and abort outcomes without retrying, and normalizes cancellation during backoff to an aborted assistant response. Coding-agent sessions and the reusable agent harness pass retry policy and callbacks into summarization, emit operation-aware retry lifecycle events, and update interactive retry indicators. Tests cover recovery, exhaustion, disabled policy, non-retryable errors, event ordering, and cancellation during backoff.
diff: The change added RetryPolicy, RetryCallbacks, abort-aware backoff, and retryAssistantCall to the AI utility layer; replaced direct single-shot completion calls in compaction, split-turn, and branch-summary paths with retry-wrapped completion choke points; threaded retry settings and callbacks from coding-agent sessions and AgentHarness call sites; added typed retry lifecycle events and interactive status handling; and added unit, harness, and issue-specific regression tests. evidence_units.claim: Before the change, coding-agent completeSummarization directly invoked completeSimple or streamFn(...).result() once, with no retry policy or callbacks.

retryAssistantCall performs an initial call plus at most maxRetries transient-error retries, with exponential delay baseDelayMs * 2^(attempt-1), and emits scheduled, attempt-start, and finished callbacks.

The retry operation returns successful and non-retryable responses immediately, never retries an aborted response, and converts cancellation during retry sleep into an AssistantMessage with stopReason "aborted".

Transient classification includes transport, connection, timeout, server, rate-limit, premature-stream, and explicit retry-guidance errors, while quota, billing, budget, and subscription-limit errors are explicitly excluded.

title: Cap shell-tool output truncation to the remaining model context budget
before: At parent commit 4f91037af49556763fe3e5bd15a71016a5b69e88, Config.getTruncateToolOutputThreshold() returned only the configured truncation threshold. Consequently, the shell-result handling call site could pass that fixed threshold to truncation even when it exceeded the model context window remaining after the last prompt.
after: At b416508ef1c64db6cdac2f185afa579368c353cf, Config.getTruncateToolOutputThreshold() returns the smaller of the configured threshold and four times the difference between the active model's token limit and the last prompt token count. The existing shell-result handling call site therefore truncates against a character estimate of the remaining context whenever that estimate is smaller, while preserving lower default or custom caps.
diff: The change imports the model token-limit resolver and UI prompt-token telemetry into the configuration module, replaces the fixed threshold getter with Math.min(4 * (tokenLimit(model) - lastPromptTokenCount), configuredThreshold), and adds three unit-test cases covering a remaining-context cap, retention of a smaller default cap, and retention or override of a custom cap. No shell scheduler code was changed; its existing threshold consumer automatically receives the adaptive value.

title: Recognize an official model alias when resolving context and output budgets
before: At parent commit 156092e892db5b098bd6d0ecf606dd37449538fe, the ordered input-limit table recognized only names beginning with `deepseek-v4` as the 1,000,000-token tier. The official `deepseek-flash` name therefore matched the later generic `deepseek` rule and resolved to 131,072 input tokens. The output table likewise recognized only `deepseek-v4`; because `deepseek-flash` matched no output-specific rule, `tokenLimit(..., 'output')` returned the 32,000-token default. Existing tests covered V4-prefixed and older-family names but not the official alias.
after: At commit 3987391392611e5d1f66851681f13ee7e55f4864, both ordered tables recognize names beginning with either `deepseek-v4` or `deepseek-flash` before their generic fallbacks. Consequently, `deepseek-flash` resolves to a 1,000,000-token input context and a 384,000-token output limit, while older DeepSeek families retain their existing 128K input and family-specific/default output behavior. A focused regression test asserts both limits for the official alias.
diff: The change replaces `/^deepseek-v4/` with `/^deepseek-(?:v4|flash)/` in the input and output limit tables, adds comments explaining the official-name alias and ordered-fallback hazard, and adds two regression assertions for `tokenLimit('deepseek-flash')` and `tokenLimit('deepseek-flash', 'output')`. commit.subject: fix(core): resolve DeepSeek's official API `deepseek-flash` name at V4 limits (#11909)
commit.body_excerpt:
The official DeepSeek API only accepts `deepseek-flash` and `deepseek-v4-pro`
as model names, but the V4 rules keyed on `/^deepseek-v4/`, so the direct-API
name fell through to the generic 128K/32K row and long sessions died on
COMPRESSION_FAILED_OUTPUT_TRUNCATED. Both rules now match
`/^deepseek-(?:v4|flash)/`; older families keep their pinned fallbacks.

Closes #11894

title: Restore persisted conversation context when starting a new session
before: At parent 1098b428e6e118be2e4ebb49a3dd2b14ae79e50e, coder initialization accepted optional in-memory completed messages but otherwise initialized an empty completed-message list. Although chat transcripts were persisted as Markdown, startup did not read or reconstruct that transcript, so a restarted session lacked prior conversational context. History summarization always used the model-defined history budget and could pass an arbitrarily large old-message head to the summarizer.
after: At merge commit 45b2ba8a1056bb27f197b01d08f3ea0d4d92b668, initialization preserves explicitly supplied completed messages, but when none exist it reads the configured chat-history file, parses persisted user and assistant turns, installs them as completed messages, and starts background compaction. Startup announcements report restored history. A command-line token-budget override is propagated to the summarizer, and the summarization path selects the newest portion of an old-message head that fits within the summarizer model's input capacity.
diff: Relative to first parent 1098b428, four implementation files changed: aider/args.py adds --max-chat-history-tokens; aider/main.py passes that option into coder construction; aider/coders/base_coder.py selects the configured or model-default budget, conditionally restores persisted history when no completed messages were supplied, starts summarization, and announces restoration; aider/history.py extracts Markdown-to-message parsing into ChatSummary and bounds the old-message subset submitted for summarization. No test file changed in the first-parent diff.

episode.title: Restore persisted conversation context when starting a new session
episode.before: At parent 1098b428e6e118be2e4ebb49a3dd2b14ae79e50e, coder initialization accepted optional in-memory completed messages but otherwise initialized an empty completed-message list. Although chat transcripts were persisted as Markdown, startup did not read or reconstruct that transcript, so a restarted session lacked prior conversational context. History summarization always used the model-defined history budget and could pass an arbitrarily large old-message head to the summarizer.
episode.after: At merge commit 45b2ba8a1056bb27f197b01d08f3ea0d4d92b668, initialization preserves explicitly supplied completed messages, but when none exist it reads the configured chat-history file, parses persisted user and assistant turns, installs them as completed messages, and starts background compaction. Startup announcements report restored history. A command-line token-budget override is propagated to the summarizer, and the summarization path selects the newest portion of an old-message head that fits within the summarizer model's input capacity.
episode.diff: Relative to first parent 1098b428, four implementation files changed: aider/args.py adds --max-chat-history-tokens; aider/main.py passes that option into coder construction; aider/coders/base_coder.py selects the configured or model-default budget, conditionally restores persisted history when no completed messages were supplied, starts summarization, and announces restoration; aider/history.py extracts Markdown-to-message parsing into ChatSummary and bounds the old-message subset submitted for summarization. No test file changed in the first-parent diff.

evidence_units.claim: The pinned ref is merge commit 45b2ba8a with first parent 1098b428 and subject 'Restore prior chat history on launch'.

Before the change, coder initialization converted an absent completed-message argument into an empty list and constructed ChatSummary from the model default, but performed no persisted-history read or restoration.

After the change, coder initialization uses an explicit history-token budget when supplied, otherwise the model default; if completed messages are empty, it reads io.chat_history_file, parses nonempty content, assigns the reconstructed messages, and invokes summarize_start().

The Markdown parser ignores transcript headings, quoted/tool output, and slash-command headings; it emits user messages from ordinary '#### ' headings and buffered assistant text as assistant messages.

When summarizing an oversized history head, the implementation walks backward from the newest old messages and retains only a subset within the summarizer model's maximum input tokens minus a 512-token reserve.
The command-line parser defines --max-chat-history-tokens with a null default, and the main construction path passes its value to the coder.
The startup announcement list includes 'Restored previous conversation history.' whenever completed messages are present after initialization.
The first-parent implementation diff changes only aider/args.py, aider/coders/base_coder.py, aider/history.py, and aider/main.py; it contains no test-file modification.
The complete first-parent patch passes Git's whitespace-error check.
The before/after diff adds persisted-history restoration without replacing explicitly supplied completed messages because the file read is guarded by an empty completed-message predicate.

title: Publish session forks and torn-tail repairs atomically
before: At parent fadb74f684aaa7755463593e0564b58f9ed081e2, torn-tail recovery rewrote the live session file directly with its valid prefix. Forking created the destination header first and then appended copied entries, lane pointers, the session name, and labels one mutation at a time. A failure during either operation could therefore expose a damaged existing session or a discoverable partial fork.
after: At a838c069e6318edee8317eff759b74c3934745f0, the filesystem abstraction supports atomic rename-and-replace. Forks and torn-tail repairs construct a complete sibling temporary file and publish it with one rename; failures remove the temporary file while leaving the destination absent or unchanged. Fork snapshot mutations are generated centrally from session state and reused by memory and JSONL storage.
diff: Added a rename operation to the execution environment; added a stage-then-rename publication helper; routed torn-tail repair and JSONL fork creation through atomic publication; moved fork selection and mutation sequencing into the session-state owner; reduced the repository layer to path/header preparation and storage delegation; added failure-injection tests for staging, rename, repair, append-queue recovery, and replay validation.

episode.title: Publish session forks and torn-tail repairs atomically
episode.before: At parent fadb74f684aaa7755463593e0564b58f9ed081e2, torn-tail recovery rewrote the live session file directly with its valid prefix. Forking created the destination header first and then appended copied entries, lane pointers, the session name, and labels one mutation at a time. A failure during either operation could therefore expose a damaged existing session or a discoverable partial fork.
episode.after: At a838c069e6318edee8317eff759b74c3934745f0, the filesystem abstraction supports atomic rename-and-replace. Forks and torn-tail repairs construct a complete sibling temporary file and publish it with one rename; failures remove the temporary file while leaving the destination absent or unchanged. Fork snapshot mutations are generated centrally from session state and reused by memory and JSONL storage.
episode.diff: Added a rename operation to the execution environment; added a stage-then-rename publication helper; routed torn-tail repair and JSONL fork creation through atomic publication; moved fork selection and mutation sequencing into the session-state owner; reduced the repository layer to path/header preparation and storage delegation; added failure-injection tests for staging, rename, repair, append-queue recovery, and replay validation.

evidence_units.claim: Commit a838c069e6318edee8317eff759b74c3934745f0 is the implementation-bearing resolution for PR/issue 7707 and has parent fadb74f684aaa7755463593e0564b58f9ed081e2.
The parent implementation repaired a torn final JSONL mutation by writing the valid prefix directly to the live session path.

The parent fork implementation created the destination session before copying entries, lanes, name, and labels through separate awaited appends, allowing intermediate destination states to become visible.
The new publication helper populates a deterministic sibling .tmp file, atomically renames it over the destination, and removes the temporary file on population or rename failure.
Torn-tail recovery now stages the valid prefix and publishes it through the atomic replacement helper instead of rewriting the live file directly.
Fork creation builds a temporary target containing the header and all selected mutations, publishes it atomically, and reloads the committed destination.
Session state now computes the complete ordered fork mutation sequence for tree or branch scope, including lane pointers, name, and labels, with fresh consecutive sequence numbers.
The repository prepares the destination identity and delegates fork publication to the source storage, while ordinary creation delegates file initialization to storage.
The execution environment implements rename-and-replace and reports a failed rename against the source path.
Filesystem tests verify that rename removes the source, replaces an existing destination, preserves the destination when the source is missing, and reports the missing source path.
Failure-injection tests verify that failed fork staging or failed atomic rename publishes no fork and leaves no temporary file.
A failure-injection test verifies that interrupted torn-tail staging preserves the original session bytes and removes the temporary file.
Fork conformance assertions verify that a reopened fork retains selected entries, lanes, name, and labels and excludes operation records.
An append failure test verifies that failed durable append does not advance in-memory state or poison the serialized write queue; the next append commits with sequence one and survives reopening.

The change modifies ten agent implementation and test files, adding 407 lines and removing 126 lines, with commit messages explicitly describing crash-safe JSONL publication and relocation of file creation, forking, and fork mutation construction.

commit.subject: Harden Code Mode tool-call completeness tracking (#44472)
commit.body_excerpt:
## Why

Reused call IDs, ambiguous exec/wait associations, and missing history can make tool-call completeness claims unreliable. Truncating one cell's recorded calls should also preserve completeness for unrelated cells.

## What changed

- Track observed call and runtime cell IDs with bounded memory, including call IDs from initial history, and withhold completeness when evidence is missing or ambiguous.
- Validate exec/wait input-output associations and keep invalidated completeness from returning on retries. Withhold wait completeness after resume or fork, where runtime cell IDs can be reused.
- Keep truncation markers and omission counts local to each output, clearing completeness across the affected cell while preserving unrelated cells within the metadata budget.
- Refresh recording

title: Halt repeated variants of read-only repository inspection commands
before: At parent 680f523853175856236162460fcd6985c9d68620, always-on loop protection recognized only consecutive tool calls with identical names and arguments plus the per-turn tool-call cap. Repeated shell inspection calls whose command strings varied could therefore avoid the identical-call guard; the broader same-tool action-stagnation heuristic was behind the skipLoopDetection gate. No shell-inspection loop type, normalized inspection bucket, streak state, or corresponding diagnostic existed.
after: At 3ce46949c2132dd8b3cc8f05cdc6c023aee0c2da, the always-on safety tier classifies read-only overview-style repository inspections into one semantic bucket, counts consecutive bucket membership, and halts at eight calls with a dedicated loop type and telemetry event. The streak resets on any nonmatching tool call and on retry, and honors the explicit session-level disable. Classification fails open for write-bearing or non-repository command chains and file-specific diffs. Existing stream handling then clears pending calls, emits LoopDetected, and stops the turn; the non-interactive CLI reports the dedicated reason and identifies it as always-on.
diff: The commit modifies five files: it adds shell-inspection classification, streak tracking, reset behavior, threshold detection, loop logging, and always-on wiring in the loop-detection service; adds the SHELL_COMMAND_STAGNATION telemetry enum; extends the non-interactive reason map and always-on hint; updates client comments describing the safety tier; and adds regression coverage for varied and newline-separated inspections, threshold behavior, resets, session disable, and false-positive boundaries for productive chains, non-repository commands, and path-specific diffs.

title: Strip truncated tool-argument markup glued to a bare tool name
before: At parent commit 41c17d9b5e1299b404700f86d6abad5cd406f3b6, the unterminated-tool-call sanitizer recognized argument tags only when the tag itself began the line, or when an argument closer ended the line. A truncated serialization such as `process_manage<arg_key>action</arg_key>...` therefore retained raw tool-contract markup because the bare tool name preceded the first argument tag.
after: At cf8b08edac3a78feb4b9db0c20a62934c3a6c49d, the sanitizer accepts an optional identifier-only prefix composed of word characters, dots, colons, or hyphens before a line-boundary argument tag. evidence_units.claim: The pinned merge commit resolves PR #5549 as an implementation-bearing change titled "feat(ui): Improved project approval settings" with 26 coding-agent files changed.

Before the change, hasProjectTrustInputs treated AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md in the directory ancestry as approval-triggering inputs, and ProjectTrustStore.get read only the exact normalized working-directory key.
After the change, trust-input detection checks the current project's .pi directory and ancestral .agents/skills directories, but no longer treats AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md as trust-gated inputs.
Project context loading no longer accepts a projectTrusted flag and always collects context files from the working directory and its ancestors.
The resource-loader regression test proves that an untrusted project still exposes its AGENTS.md while extensions, skills, prompts, themes, and project settings remain excluded.

The trust store normalizes paths, walks toward the filesystem root to find the nearest explicit decision, reports the source path, and supports locked multi-path updates that can delete child overrides.
Trust choices now include trusting the current folder, trusting its parent while clearing the current override, session-only allow/deny choices, and persistent denial.
Trust-manager tests prove nearest-ancestor inheritance, child override precedence, and restoration of parent inheritance after atomically clearing the child override.
Trust-selector tests prove inherited-decision labeling and that selecting parent trust returns coordinated parent-save and child-clear updates.

The shared resolver orders trust policy as explicit override, automatic approval when no gated inputs exist, extension hook, persisted nearest-path decision, global ask/always/never default, and finally UI selection or fail-closed denial when no UI or selection is available.
The global settings manager exposes defaultProjectTrust with ask as the fallback for absent or invalid values and persists changes only in global settings.
Settings tests prove that project-local settings cannot override the global default trust policy and that invalid values resolve to ask.
The resource loader provides a bootstrap pass that forces untrusted settings before loading only the current safe extension set, then reloads full resources after trust resolution.

Package and config commands construct an initially untrusted settings manager, optionally load bootstrap trust extensions, invoke the shared resolver, set the resulting trust state, report warnings, and block local package mutations when untrusted.
Normal application startup invokes the shared resolver with the global default, bootstrap extensions, UI context, and extension-error reporting before resource loading continues.

Package-command tests prove that the global always policy enables project packages, project_trust extensions can approve package commands, and an explicit trust-store denial overrides the global always policy.
The parent implementation embedded trust resolution in main and used a separate package-command rule, while the new implementation extracts the resolver and routes both command paths through it.

title: Fail closed when restricted shell-command arguments cannot be parsed in automatic-approval mode
before: At parent cfd7541ad45b25109744c988ac5fc8128accb0ec, shell-command policy evaluation treated only an empty parsed-command list as a parsing failure. after: At ed469e492b4190ce8983b9dd1c5fb5b9f1b140d0, an empty parsed-command list or parser-reported error enters the failure path. Existing explicit DENY decisions remain DENY. title: Broaden approved-command writes without weakening explicit filesystem denials
before: At parent de9e78e3e7caed0fdd75d20ae617faa646dfef3c, there was no executor-context operation that safely derived an approved-command filesystem policy by widening writes while retaining explicit path and glob read denials. Linux bubblewrap consumed separately resolved writable and unreadable roots; a writable bind of `/` could shadow the previously created minimal `/dev`, separate writable root-metadata mounts could follow symlinks and reopen denied targets, and deny-root resolution retained only effective targets rather than the literal paths needed to detect writable-symlink crossings. The execution capability contract also had no flags distinguishing support for these Linux behaviors.
after: At 645b683a9e712ae6d90a364e3cf597466e4146d0, restricted policies can be transformed for approved commands into root-wide and permitted root-metadata writes while preserving explicit path and glob denials. Transformation fails closed by returning the original policy when workspace-root denials cannot be materialized, the filesystem root cannot be determined, a deny matcher cannot be built, or the root itself is denied. Linux mount preparation inherits root-metadata access from a writable root, preserves literal deny paths, skips redundant aliases of `/`, recreates standard devices after binding `/`, and applies deny masks afterward. Executors advertise the two Linux guarantees through backward-compatible opt-in capability fields.
diff: The commit adds `FileSystemSandboxPolicy::for_approved_command`; adds Linux-specific writable-root and unreadable-root projections that prevent metadata remount and symlink-denial bypasses; changes bubblewrap mount construction to use those projections, avoid duplicate root-alias binds, and restore `/dev` after a writable root bind; adds two default-false, omitted-when-false capability fields; and adds policy, Windows volume, bubblewrap argument-order, standard-device, and root-metadata symlink regression tests. The commit changes 9 files with 780 insertions and 12 deletions.

commit.subject: Preserve filesystem denials when preparing approved commands (#48155)
commit.body_excerpt:
## Why

Approved commands need broader write access while retaining explicit read denials. On Linux, binding the filesystem root writable can shadow standard devices, and additional root-metadata mounts can reopen denied symlink targets.

## What changed

- Add `FileSystemSandboxPolicy::for_approved_command` to grant root and root-metadata writes while retaining path and glob denials. Keep the original policy when denials cannot be resolved or deny the root.
- Restore standard devices after Linux writable root binds, then apply explicit deny masks. Avoid redundant root-alias binds and inherit root-metadata writes from the root mount so denied targets stay masked.
- Preserve literal deny paths alongside resolved targets so Linux can reject denials that cross writable symlinks.
- Advertise L

commit.subject: Preserve filesystem denials when preparing approved commands (#48155)
commit.body_excerpt:
## Why

Approved commands need broader write access while retaining explicit read denials. On Linux, binding the filesystem root writable can shadow standard devices, and additional root-metadata mounts can reopen denied symlink targets.

## What changed

- Add `FileSystemSandboxPolicy::for_approved_command` to grant root and root-metadata writes while retaining path and glob denials. Keep the original policy when denials cannot be resolved or deny the root.
- Restore standard devices after Linux writable root binds, then apply explicit deny masks. Avoid redundant root-alias binds and inherit root-metadata writes from the root mount so denied targets stay masked.
- Preserve literal deny paths alongside resolved targets so Linux can reject denials that cross writable symlinks.
- Advertise L

episode.title: Broaden approved-command writes without weakening explicit filesystem denials
episode.before: At parent de9e78e3e7caed0fdd75d20ae617faa646dfef3c, there was no executor-context operation that safely derived an approved-command filesystem policy by widening writes while retaining explicit path and glob read denials. Linux bubblewrap consumed separately resolved writable and unreadable roots; a writable bind of `/` could shadow the previously created minimal `/dev`, separate writable root-metadata mounts could follow symlinks and reopen denied targets, and deny-root resolution retained only effective targets rather than the literal paths needed to detect writable-symlink crossings. The execution capability contract also had no flags distinguishing support for these Linux behaviors.
episode.after: At 645b683a9e712ae6d90a364e3cf597466e4146d0, restricted policies can be transformed for approved commands into root-wide and permitted root-metadata writes while preserving explicit path and glob denials. Transformation fails closed by returning the original policy when workspace-root denials cannot be materialized, the filesystem root cannot be determined, a deny matcher cannot be built, or the root itself is denied. Linux mount preparation inherits root-metadata access from a writable root, preserves literal deny paths, skips redundant aliases of `/`, recreates standard devices after binding `/`, and applies deny masks afterward. Executors advertise the two Linux guarantees through backward-compatible opt-in capability fields.
episode.diff: The commit adds `FileSystemSandboxPolicy::for_approved_command`; adds Linux-specific writable-root and unreadable-root projections that prevent metadata remount and symlink-denial bypasses; changes bubblewrap mount construction to use those projections, avoid duplicate root-alias binds, and restore `/dev` after a writable root bind; adds two default-false, omitted-when-false capability fields; and adds policy, Windows volume, bubblewrap argument-order, standard-device, and root-metadata symlink regression tests. The commit changes 9 files with 780 insertions and 12 deletions.

evidence_units.claim: Commit 645b683a states that approved commands require broader write access while retaining explicit read denials, and identifies Linux root binds shadowing devices and metadata mounts reopening denied symlink targets as the failures being corrected.
The pinned commit changes nine files, adding 780 lines and removing 12, including policy transformation, Linux mount construction, capability protocol, and regression tests.

`for_approved_command` starts from a restricted root-write policy, copies deny-read restrictions, materializes project-root references, validates a strict deny matcher, grants protected root-metadata writes only where not denied, and returns the original policy whenever safe materialization or root validation fails.

The policy layer adds a writable-root projection that suppresses separate protected-metadata mounts when `/` is writable, and an unreadable-root projection that retains literal deny paths alongside resolved targets for restricted policies.

Linux bubblewrap construction switches to the new writable and unreadable projections, detects a writable `/` bind, skips aliases resolving back to `/`, recreates the minimal `/dev` and `/dev/shm` after the root bind, and then applies explicit masks.

Policy tests cover Unix, Windows-drive, and UNC contexts; prove that root and allowed metadata become writable while explicit path and glob denials remain effective; and prove that root-denying or unresolvable denials leave the original policy unchanged.

The Windows sandbox policy test proves volume-root expansion grants writes on discovered volumes without restoring prior read/write grants, while retained denials and explicitly denied root metadata remain denied.

The managed-proxy Linux integration test runs an approved policy that can use `/dev/null`, `/dev/zero`, and `/dev/urandom` and write an output file, while reading the explicitly denied secret still fails with permission denied.

The root-metadata integration test proves metadata symlinks cannot reopen a denied directory, allowed metadata remains writable, writable-symlink crossings are rejected, and an explicit nested writable carveout reopens only that nested area.

The execution protocol adds two default-false capability flags for preserving devices under Linux root writes and preserving restrictions under approved root writes; false values are omitted from serialization and local Linux executors advertise both.
Protocol tests prove legacy capability payloads deserialize with both new flags false, false flags are absent on the wire, and independently enabled or fully enabled payloads round-trip.

The parent version lacks `for_approved_command`, the root-metadata inheritance mode, literal-path-preserving unreadable roots, root-bind device restoration, root-alias suppression, and the two capability fields.

title: Recover reasoning-only incomplete turns by failing over without leaking protocol-specific replay state
before: At parent d45fd1aa31e54e411a0df2661849ccb255c22ed6, an incomplete Codex Responses turn used one bare replay and then a synthetic continuation nudge, but all incomplete responses shared one three-attempt counter. On the third incomplete response, even when every response contained only internal reasoning and no visible answer or tool call, the turn reset the counter, persisted the transcript, and returned a terminal partial result. It did not classify this condition as a failover reason, activate a configured fallback, grant a bounded call when the iteration budget was exhausted, rebind the system prompt to the fallback identity, or remove the Codex-only nudge when assembling a request for another protocol.
after: At merge commit 656eb283096c979ae4e6dc454920c2038e622990, the turn maintains a separate consecutive reasoning-only streak, resetting it when visible output or a normal response breaks the streak. The third consecutive incomplete response with neither visible text nor a tool call activates the next configured fallback using the semantic reason incomplete_response. If the trigger consumed the iteration budget, exactly one grace call is armed so the fallback can answer. Response intake then refreshes the active system prompt after failover and continues the same turn. When the destination uses a different protocol, request assembly drops both thinking-only replay rows and the synthetic continuation nudge before merging adjacent user rows, preserving valid role alternation. If no fallback is available, the existing terminal partial-result path remains.
diff: The change adds an incomplete_response failover category and per-turn reasoning-only streak state; extends incomplete-response continuation to distinguish visible partials from reasoning-only stalls, activate fallback after three consecutive stalls, and arm one bounded grace call; propagates a fallback-activated control result through response intake so the system prompt is synchronized before retrying; extends transcript normalization with an optional exact nudge marker and applies it only on cross-protocol requests; and adds focused tests for successful fallback with one grace call, streak behavior after visible partial output, cross-protocol cleanup and role alternation, plus enum coverage and fixture initialization.

title: Resume partially delivered streams after retryable socket closure without duplicating output
before: At parent commit 3d1eba935f6a75d9e67adf667002700c5c592ec2, the stream loop could replay a request only when the current attempt had produced no non-thought content. If a retryable socket-level transport error occurred after visible answer text had reached the caller, replay was rejected to avoid duplication and the transport error propagated. Text-only partial output was not durable history, so there was no continuation path that both preserved the caller's visible prefix and reconstructed the complete model turn.
after: At d7c0d4ca7706ede8d1c8877a20343aa3e1d40bf5, retryable transport cuts with accumulated nonblank text and no function call enter a separately budgeted continuation path. Each continuation request temporarily appends the delivered model prefix and a fenced resume instruction, emits a continuation RETRY so consumers retain displayed text, deduplicates overlap at attempt boundaries, and merges the delivered prefix into the successful trailing model turn. Fresh-restart retries and reactive compression clear staged continuation state; function-call cuts and exhausted continuation budgets still propagate.
diff: The change adds a three-attempt continuation budget and shared recovery-message construction; tracks per-attempt and accumulated delivered text plus function-call presence; distinguishes clean replay from continuation using accumulated visible output; creates request-only synthetic continuation turns; emits continuation-aware retry events; resets staged state whenever another recovery branch restarts from rebuilt/original contents; folds repeated overlap between attempts; and prepends the recovered prefix into durable history. The test suite adds scenarios for successful continuation, history reconstruction, repeated cuts, overlap removal, thought-only or empty later attempts, budget exhaustion, function-call exclusion, clean replay cases, and continuation supersession by other retry paths.

    * fix(core): resume long streams cut by a socket-level close
    
    Long generations that are cut mid-response by a gateway SSE idle timeout
    (DashScope closes at ~3-5 min) failed outright, however many retries were
    configured. The stream retry loop could only recover by *replaying* the
    request, and that path is gated on `!streamYieldedChunk` — by the time a
    long answer is cut, chunks have obviously been delivered, so the gate was
    shut exactly when recovery was needed.
    
    Two changes:
    
    - Widen the replay gate from "any chunk yielded" to "visible output
      yielded" (non-blank answer text or a functionCall). Thinking models emit
      reasoning within seconds, which made replay unreachable for the very
      generations that need it. The UI's non-continuation RETRY handler clears
      the thought buffer, and the rate-limit and invalid-stream branches
      already re-send after thoughts have streamed, so this matches existing
      behaviour rather than adding risk.
    
    - Add continuation recovery for cuts that already delivered answer text,
      where replaying would duplicate what the caller has on screen. Keep the
      delivered text, ask the model to resume from it, and emit
      `{ RETRY, isContinuation: true }` so the UI keeps its text buffer — the
      same shape the MAX_TOKENS truncation path already uses. The synthetic
      turns are built into the request only, never written to `history`, so
      they cannot leak into the transcript or a later compression; on success
      the delivered prefix is merged back into the trailing model turn, with
      replayed overlap deduped by the existing recovery helper. Budget of 3,
      since one generation can be cut repeatedly by the same timeout.
    
    Cuts that delivered a `functionCall` are excluded: injecting a user turn
    between a `functionCall` and its `functionResponse` yields a sequence
    providers reject, and the scheduler's repair path already covers it.
    
    Fixes #7832
    
    * fix(core): reset continuation state on every fresh-restart retry
    
    Review found that the `suppressNextRetryEvent` arm bypasses the
    continuation reset. Two branches emit a non-continuation RETRY *and* set
    `suppressNextRetryEvent`, so the next loop iteration takes the suppress
    arm and skips the `else if` that clears the staged continuation:
    
    - the transport replay branch, reachable when a continuation attempt is
      itself cut before yielding visible output, and
    - the reactive compression branch, which is if anything more likely on a
      continuation attempt, since that request carries the delivered text and
      the resume instruction on top of the original contents.
    
    Either way the UI has dropped the delivered text (plain RETRY) while the
    request still asks the model to resume from it, and the merge on success
    writes that discarded text back into history — a permanent UI/history
    mismatch visible on `/compress` and `--resume`.
    
    Extract the reset into `resetTransportContinuation()` and call it from
    both branches before they set the flag. Resetting inside the suppress arm
    instead would clear the state of a continuation that is legitimately in
    flight.
    
    The pre-existing supersession test used `InvalidStreamError`, whose retry
    branch does not set `suppressNextRetryEvent`, so it exercised the
    `else if` path and neither trigger. Add a test per branch; both fail if
    their reset is removed.
    
    * fix(core): dedup replayed overlap when an intermediate cut is continued
    
    The continuation buffer accumulated each attempt's delivered text with a
    raw `+=`. Overlap dedup ran only at merge time, comparing the *final*
    attempt against the buffer, so an overlap replayed by an intermediate
    attempt was never stripped: it was baked into the buffer, sent in every
    later request, and merged into durable history.
    
    Reachable because maxContinuationRetries is 3, so two cuts fit in one
    send. Attempt 1 delivers "part one " and is cut; attempt 2 replays its
    tail as "part one part two " and is cut too. The buffer became
    "part one part one part two " — corrupting /compress, --resume, and the
    context of every later turn.
    
    The fix folds one attempt at a time. A per-attempt buffer collects the
    running attempt's text, and the catch path folds it into the accumulated
    buffer through getRecoveryContinuationSuffix, stripping whatever that
    attempt replayed. Deduping per chunk instead would be wrong: the overlap
    scan is suffix-anchored, so it would eat legitimately repeated text
    mid-stream. The attempt boundary is the only place a replay can occur.
    
    Also covers the two untested branches of the delivered-text merge, both
    of which already behaved correctly: a continuation leading with a thought
    part (the text merges into the text part, not ahead of the thinking) and
    one that finishes with only a thought part (the delivered text is
    inserted after it). Without coverage a regression in the insert position
    would silently misplace text in history.
    
    276 tests pass in geminiChat.test.ts; tsc and eslint clean.
    
    * fix(core): keep continuing when a later attempt is cut before it delivers
    
    The replay gate tests `!streamYieldedContentChunk`, which is declared inside
    the attempt loop and therefore per-attempt. That cannot distinguish "nothing
    has been delivered to the caller" from "this attempt was cut before delivering
    anything, after earlier attempts already put text on screen" — and only the
    first is replayable. Because the replay branch is checked before the
    continuation branch, the second case fell into it: `resetTransportContinuation()`
    dropped the accumulated text and a plain RETRY (no `isContinuation`) told the UI
    to discard output the user was watching, after which the model regenerated it
    from scratch.
    
    Reachable two ways once a continuation is in flight, both with
    `transportStreamRetryCount` still 0 so the replay budget is intact:
    
      - attempt 1 delivers "part one " -> continuation; attempt 2 is cut while
        still in its thinking phase, so it yields only a thought part and
        `streamYieldedContentChunk` is false;
      - the same, with attempt 2 cut having yielded nothing at all.
    
    Gate the replay branch on the accumulated buffer being empty as well. The two
    gates are now exact complements (`=== 0` here, `> 0` on the continuation
    branch), so a retryable transport cut after any delivered text always
    continues and never replays. The `resetTransportContinuation()` call inside the
    branch now has nothing to clear; it stays as an assertion of that invariant so
    a future gate change cannot leak staged text into a restarted attempt.
    
    `drops a pending continuation when a replay takes over` asserted the old
    behaviour for the yielded-nothing case — it was written to pin the design's
    internal consistency, not a user-visible requirement, and that premise is what
    this fixes. Rewritten as `keeps continuing when a later attempt is cut with
    nothing yielded`, asserting the delivered text survives into the third request
    and into history. The sibling tests covering the *other* plain-RETRY paths
    (fresh-restart retry, reactive compression) are unchanged and still pass:
    those genuinely do discard the delivered text, and reaching them still resets.
    
    Also extracts the resume instruction shared verbatim by
    OUTPUT_RECOVERY_MESSAGE and TRANSPORT_CONTINUATION_MESSAGE into
    RECOVERY_RESUME_INSTRUCTION. Only the lead-in sentence naming the cause
    differed, so tuning the wording on one path silently left the other on the old
    text. Both resulting strings are byte-identical to before.
    
    277 tests pass in geminiChat.test.ts; both new tests verified failing without
    the source change. tsc --noEmit and eslint clean.
    
    * docs(core): correct the foldTransportAttemptText call-site comment
    
    The comment claimed the fold runs on both exits from an attempt. It runs
    only in the catch block; the success exit merges the continuation prefix
    into history and breaks without folding.
    
    No behaviour change — every read of the accumulated buffer is inside the
    catch, after the fold. But the comment would mislead anyone adding a
    post-loop read, which would silently omit the last attempt's text, so the
    note now says which exit folds and what a new reader would have to do.

title: Honor server retry advice without restarting its countdown
before: At parent commit ab021e9f137c9daacf6ae06a495f3c7d6199fab2, the HTTP retry loop ignored Retry-After and always slept for locally computed backoff. Higher-level errors stored an optional relative Duration, so time spent transporting, mapping, reporting, or exhausting a retry could effectively restart the server-advised wait.
after: At commit 9d8de196748b57d7f463a7757eaa447b6483a331, Retry-After delay-seconds and HTTP-date values are captured as a monotonic deadline when advice is received. That deadline is carried through transport, API, protocol, provider-specific, stream-retry, and exhausted-retry error paths. HTTP and stream retries sleep until the original deadline, use local backoff only when advice is absent, and retain expired advice as an explicit zero remaining delay.
diff: Introduced the RetryAfter deadline value and header parser; attached it to HTTP transport errors; replaced relative retry-delay fields with deadline-bearing advice across API and protocol errors; preserved it during generic and provider-specific error mapping; changed HTTP and response-stream retry scheduling to sleep until the captured deadline; retained the deadline in exhausted response-retry state; and added unit and integration tests for parsing, countdown, expiry, propagation, delayed notification, ordinary response retries, and remote compaction retries.

commit.subject: Honor Retry-After and preserve server retry deadlines (#47641)
commit.body_excerpt:
## Why

HTTP retries used local backoff even when the server supplied `Retry-After`. Relative retry delays also failed to account for time spent propagating errors or reporting retries.

## What changed

- Parse `Retry-After` delay seconds and HTTP dates into a monotonic deadline captured when response headers arrive.
- Honor that deadline for HTTP retries, falling back to local backoff when valid advice is absent.
- Preserve deadlines through API and Bedrock error mapping, stream retries, and exhausted retry state. Expired advice remains a zero delay instead of triggering local backoff.

## Testing

Add coverage for header parsing, deadline countdown and expiry, error mapping after exhausted HTTP retries, and delayed stream retry notifications. Update Responses and remote compaction tests

## Why

HTTP retries used local backoff even when the server supplied `Retry-After`. Relative retry delays also failed to account for time spent propagating errors or reporting retries.

## What changed

- Parse `Retry-After` delay seconds and HTTP dates into a monotonic deadline captured when response headers arrive.
- Honor that deadline for HTTP retries, falling back to local backoff when valid advice is absent.
- Preserve deadlines through API and Bedrock error mapping, stream retries, and exhausted retry state. Expired advice remains a zero delay instead of triggering local backoff.

## Testing

Add coverage for header parsing, deadline countdown and expiry, error mapping after exhausted HTTP retries, and delayed stream retry notifications. Update Responses and remote compaction tests

limitations: No fabricated GitHub discussion metadata; implementation evidence must come from local git and checkout.

episode.title: Honor server retry advice without restarting its countdown
episode.before: At parent commit ab021e9f137c9daacf6ae06a495f3c7d6199fab2, the HTTP retry loop ignored Retry-After and always slept for locally computed backoff. Higher-level errors stored an optional relative Duration, so time spent transporting, mapping, reporting, or exhausting a retry could effectively restart the server-advised wait.
episode.after: At commit 9d8de196748b57d7f463a7757eaa447b6483a331, Retry-After delay-seconds and HTTP-date values are captured as a monotonic deadline when advice is received. That deadline is carried through transport, API, protocol, provider-specific, stream-retry, and exhausted-retry error paths. HTTP and stream retries sleep until the original deadline, use local backoff only when advice is absent, and retain expired advice as an explicit zero remaining delay.
episode.diff: Introduced the RetryAfter deadline value and header parser; attached it to HTTP transport errors; replaced relative retry-delay fields with deadline-bearing advice across API and protocol errors; preserved it during generic and provider-specific error mapping; changed HTTP and response-stream retry scheduling to sleep until the captured deadline; retained the deadline in exhausted response-retry state; and added unit and integration tests for parsing, countdown, expiry, propagation, delayed notification, ordinary response retries, and remote compaction retries.

evidence_units.claim: The pinned implementation commit identifies the defect as HTTP retries using local backoff despite Retry-After and relative delays failing to account for propagation or reporting time; it states that the fix parses advice into a monotonic deadline and preserves it through retry paths.

RetryAfter represents the earliest advised follow-up time as a Tokio Instant, parses nonnegative delay seconds or HTTP dates, exposes the original deadline, and saturates expired remaining delay to zero.
Before the change, the HTTP retry loop contained an explicit TODO to respect Retry-After, always computed local backoff, and slept for that relative duration.
The HTTP transport captures Retry-After from response headers before consuming the body and stores the resulting advice on non-success TransportError::Http values.
The HTTP retry loop now uses the captured advice when present, records its remaining delay, and sleeps until its original deadline; local backoff remains the fallback only when advice is absent.

The protocol error representation changed from an optional relative Duration to an optional RetryAfter deadline; remaining server delay is derived at observation time, and expired advice remains Some(Duration::ZERO).

API-to-protocol error mapping extracts retry advice before changing error details and reapplies the same RetryAfter value to the mapped error, including retryable, rate-limit, overload, and HTTP transport errors.
Provider-specific expired-signature remapping preserves the original retry deadline while replacing the user-facing error details.

Response-stream retry handling reads the preserved deadline, performs notification work, recomputes the remaining telemetry delay, sleeps until the original deadline, and stores that deadline when retries are exhausted.
Parser tests verify delay-seconds countdown, HTTP-date handling, explicit zero and expired dates as valid zero-delay advice, and rejection of malformed or overflowing values.
A paused-time stream test delays retry notification and verifies that the retry resumes at the original server deadline rather than waiting the full relative duration after notification completes.
An exhausted-HTTP-retry test verifies that the last captured deadline survives API error mapping, counts down across elapsed time, and remains present with zero remaining delay after expiry.

End-to-end response retry coverage returns a 503 with Retry-After: 1, verifies HTTP-layer retry telemetry, waits at least the advised interval, completes successfully, and observes exactly two requests.
Remote compaction coverage verifies that a 503 carrying Retry-After is retried at the HTTP layer after the advised interval and that compaction completes through the subsequent successful response.
A provider-specific test verifies that rewriting an expired-signature error retains the exact RetryAfter value.

candidate_atomics.name: capture-server-retry-deadline
candidate_atomics.description: Normalize server retry advice into one monotonic deadline at the point where the advice is received.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent elapsed processing time or wall-clock changes from restarting or corrupting a server-advised retry interval.
semantic_action.pre_state: A failed response or streamed error supplies retry advice as delay seconds, an HTTP date, or a parsed relative delay.
semantic_action.post_state: Valid advice is represented by one monotonic deadline captured at receipt; expired or explicit-zero advice remains valid with zero remaining delay, while invalid advice is absent.
semantic_action.validation: Paused-time parser tests verify countdown and expiry; date and malformed-value cases verify accepted and rejected input forms.

candidate_atomics.name: preserve-retry-deadline-across-error-transforms
candidate_atomics.description: Carry the original deadline through error classification, wrapping, provider adaptation, and exhausted-retry state without converting it back to a fresh duration.

semantic_action.intent: Keep retry timing semantics intact while errors cross abstraction boundaries or receive new user-facing details.
semantic_action.pre_state: An error contains a captured server retry deadline and must be mapped, wrapped, reclassified, or retained after retry exhaustion.
semantic_action.post_state: The transformed error or recovery state contains the same original deadline; querying remaining delay reflects elapsed time and returns zero after expiry instead of losing the advice.
semantic_action.validation: Exhausted-retry mapping and provider-specific remapping tests assert deadline identity, countdown, and post-expiry preservation.

candidate_atomics.name: schedule-http-retry-at-server-deadline
candidate_atomics.description: Prefer the captured server deadline for retryable HTTP failures and use local backoff only when valid advice is absent.

semantic_action.intent: Honor server load-control timing while retaining recovery for responses that provide no valid retry advice.
semantic_action.pre_state: A retry policy admits another HTTP attempt after a retryable failure, with either captured server advice or no advice.
semantic_action.post_state: With advice, the next request is delayed until the original server deadline; without advice, the configured local backoff determines the delay.
semantic_action.validation: Response and remote-compaction integration tests inject Retry-After on an overload response, observe HTTP retry telemetry, verify the advised wait, and confirm successful subsequent requests.

candidate_atomics.name: schedule-stream-retry-with-elapsed-work-accounted
candidate_atomics.description: Use the original deadline after retry reporting or other asynchronous work, and retain it when stream retries are exhausted.

semantic_action.intent: Ensure notification, error propagation, and recovery bookkeeping consume part of the server-advised wait instead of postponing recovery by a new full interval.
semantic_action.pre_state: A retryable stream error carries a server deadline, and recovery may perform asynchronous reporting or reach its retry limit before resuming or returning the error.
semantic_action.post_state: An admitted retry sleeps only until the original deadline, while an exhausted retry records and returns that same deadline for later recovery decisions.
semantic_action.validation: A virtual-time test blocks retry notification and proves resumption occurs at the original deadline; exhausted-retry coverage proves the deadline survives subsequent error mapping and expiry.

candidate_workflows.name: preserve-and-honor-server-retry-timing
candidate_workflows.description: Resolve retry-timing drift by capturing server advice once, preserving its deadline across every error boundary, and making HTTP and stream recovery schedule against that deadline while retaining local fallback only for absent advice.

workflow_graph.goal: Make all relevant retry paths honor one server-defined earliest retry instant without restarting the countdown during error propagation or reporting.
workflow_graph.entry_state: Retryable HTTP or streaming failures may contain server advice, but HTTP retries use local backoff and higher layers represent advice as a relative duration that can be restarted after elapsed processing.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Valid advice is captured once as a monotonic deadline, survives all applicable error transformations and exhausted states, drives HTTP and stream retry timing, and remains distinguishable from absent advice after expiry.
unresolved_or_deferred: The implementation leaves a TODO for preserving retry advice when reading an unbounded error body itself fails without reclassifying that failure as an HTTP-status error.
The bundle does not include PR reviews or status-check results, so validation is grounded in committed test code rather than external CI evidence.

unresolved_questions: The GitHub bundle lacks the issue/PR body, comments, reviews, timeline, and status checks.
The checkout was inspected statically at the pinned commit; no test execution result was supplied by the evidence bundle.

The workflow edge from HTTP scheduling to stream scheduling reflects the observed layered recovery path, but HTTP-only and stream-originated advice can exercise the two scheduler actions independently.
